text_fidelity_a:
FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player I bought this primarily to listen to Podcasts and some music while swimming laps. When it arrived, I was pleased with the hardware quality and ease of use. I loaded up some music and Podcasts and headed for the pool. It was relatively easy to clip the units to my goggles. The controls could be better, but are not terrible. I put it on, started playing a Podcast, put in my earplugs and started swimming. I had been concerned that my goggles might leak or come off during turns with these units clipped on, but it was not a problem at all.
The problem, though, was the sound. If sitting perfectly still underwater, it sounds decent. Pretty much on par with my 30-year-old one-speaker clock radio. However, even with earplugs, the noise of swimming and rushing water overpowers it. If I play familiar songs I can tell what I am listening to and somewhat enjoy them. However, forget about the spoken word. I had to turn the volume up really loud to be able to make out most of what was said on the Podcast due to distortion and background noise. And then it was just too loud to be enjoyable. In fact, I am sure that others in the pool could hear some sound from it. I tried to adjust it in every possible way, and followed the instructions precisely.
This seems like a good idea, but I am disappointed, especially for the cost.

Pros: Solid design, no earphones or earbuds, can still wear earplugs, easy to wear, stays on goggles and doesn't pull them off, easy to load songs.
Cons: Price, 1 GB of storage is a total insult, limited features and controls for an MP3 player, poor sound quality overshadows all else.
text_fidelity_b: FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player

text_fidelity_a:
Green Guru Gear Dutchy Bike Bicycle Bike Upcycled Made in USA Pannier Bag (design may vary) I did not purchase these on Amazon, but direct from the sellers (Green Guru Gear) website. I got an EBike (Aventon Pace 500) for commuting to work and needed something to hold my personal items for a post-ride, pre-work shower. These pannier bags fill the need excellently. You can hold a lot of items in there. Everything I can fit in my gym bag, which is pretty big, I can fit in these two panniers. In addition, I can fit my full lunch bag as well. My feet do not hit the bags when I peddle. If I choose to, I could also fit my purse/backpack in them, but I carry that on my back just for more security when I ride.

I had a Topeak MTX Quick track rear rack installed on my bike to use the MTX basket with and these panniers fit perfectly on them. I can actually use the panniers and the basket at the same time because the hooks on the panniers are flush with the top of the bags and the tops of the bags are level with the top of the rack itself, so the basket can slide onto the Quick track easily with the panniers in place. So if you have even more stuff to haul on the bicycle you have all that extra space with the basket as well. Double check the weight limits on the bags and the rack before you do that though.

I knew the print on the panniers would be randomly selected when I placed my order, but I did note that they mentioned that they will try and match them if you purchase a pair, they did pretty good as both of them were in nice brown tones with pretty cool pictures/patterns on them. The bags are pretty simple to install on the rack, just hook them on and I wrap the bottom securing hook around the rack supports and hook it on sideways. The bags do not come out or off even if I go over big bumps in the road. As far as I can see about its "waterproof-ness" the material used on the cover and the front bottom half of the bags look more water "resistant", if its a few sprinkles or a light rain, it would hold up, but not a continuous downpour, especially since the sides of the bag don't appear to be water proof/resistant. The cover is secured to the front of the bag by hook & loop (Velcro) patches, they are pretty strong but cannot be locked, so if you require extra security get some type of cover to go over or secure it even more with bungee cords/nets. If you are so inclined, you could even sew on some straps with securing clips on them.

If I don't use the basket with the bags, they are easy to remove and carry. Carry by the short handles or the adjustable and convenient shoulder straps as well. They fold up for easy, low profile storage when not in use, either on the bike rack or somewhere else. I would not leave these unattended on a bicycle, they are so nice that someone may be tempted to steal them (probably those same crumbs that take the bicycle lights if you don't take them with you). If I use the basket also, it will have to be removed before removing the bags.

Overall, I am happy with my purchase of the Green Guru Dutchy pannier bags, I would recommend them for anyone considering getting panniers for your bicycle rack(s). They are great looking on the bicycle and pretty unique from other panniers.
text_fidelity_b: Green Guru Gear Dutchy Bike Bicycle Bike Upcycled Made in USA Pannier Bag (design may vary)

Gearhandle Black Hydration Pack Lanyard Drink Tube Clip I use my hydration packs on hikes, and I have one on the back of my computer chair. I've use the snap-on spring clips and the magnetic types before with success, but they typically are not designed to fit around an insulation sleeve, so I thought I'd try this. For me, it didn't work - the lanyard just doesn't keep the hydration tube in place. It might corral it, which is useful, but the tube tends to slip within the lanyard with only moderate jostling back and forth.

That would earn it three stars, but the plastic clip broke after maybe a week on the back of my chair - not even along a seam, just across one of the flat jaws. That, and the clip isn't even all that secure - there's no lock that keeps it tight, it just sort of rotates into a closed position and you have to hope it doesn't un-rotate again.

Altogether, would not recommend. The magnetic clip or the spring clips are are a better choice, even if you have to cut a little slot into your insulation sleeve to make it fit.

SANSBUG 1-Person Popup Screen Tent (Tarp Floor) This net is great and can even be used as a one person tent in clear weather. This seals completely, unlike the big hanging nets that hang down around you but leave the floor or ground exposed.

Setup takes all of 10 seconds, including taking the tent out of the bag and throwing the tent in the air to let it pop up on its own. You don't have to worry about tying anything off, but it does come with stakes if you want to use it outdoors as tent. Storage is easy and it folds float in about a 30" ring.

I'm 5'9" tall and overweight, and I had plenty of leg room and room on either side and could sit up and move around inside the tent. I also have room for a few vital pieces of gear that I wanted to keep with me. If your over 6' tall your mileage may vary.

I set my tent up on a cot at our local Boy Scout summer camp inside a permanent canvass tent that didn't completely seal. It fit pretty well on the cot, with just a little overhang on either side of the cot.

My son and his tent mate each had one of these, and they had to reposition their cots so they ran from side to side instead of front to back to avoid downward pressure from the sloping tent roof. The sloping ends of this cot then fit the roofline of the tent very well.

I have slept in this for 3 nights so far and my son has slept in his 6 nights. It seems well made and like it will hold up well.
text_fidelity_b: SANSBUG 1-Person Popup Screen Tent (Tarp Floor)

text_fidelity_a:
Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce I really hate being the first and only 4 star review but here goes..

I got mine from RawReform, whom I dearly love, and was pleased to get it very quickly and loved all the goodies that came with it.
I HIGHLY recommend that you watch the DVD on the immune system that came with it - very interesting and well done informationally. Mine also came with a book, "Rebounding For Better Health" which I also recommend reading. This book enlightened me and I learned so much from just reading this very simple book!
I'm also glad I did as I learned the importance of 'bouncing' before you 'jump'; and what great benefit the 'health bounce' has for your body!

I completely concur with the other reviewers on the quality of the Needak and would never advise buying BELOW this quality standard. I have not tried folding it yet, so I cannot comment on the ease of doing so. (Unfolding was easy.)

(I had an entire review written and almost completed when my computer fritzed, so I'm trying to remember all the points I had previously written.)

There were a few reviews in particular that cinched the deal and 'sold' me on getting mine. I had recently been troubled with hip problems that a Chiropractor had made MUCH worse (not ALL chiros, just this one) and was getting concerned about my hip/knee pain. My normal forms of exercise were also making it worse and so I wanted to see how rebounding would help.
Let me tell you that with just a couple minutes here and a couple minutes there of doing the 'health bounce' alone has made remarkable differences in my hip/knee pain (almost gone); noticeable improvements in the 'elimination' area; and giving me deeper, restful sleep and less irritability. AND, I've even noticed a slimmer tummy!
Now, how can this be??!!! I'm only doing a COUPLE minutes here and there!
Yet, the book and the DVD will explain how this form of body movement affects your body at the deepest level - the CELLULAR level!
With that information - with those results - how is it that people aren't STAMPEDING and buying these things faster than Amazon can sell their KINDLES!!??
I think it's just a matter of time, and they will.
I realized I had been in the 'dark' too long to not have known the incredible benefits that rebounding/bouncing does for your health, but not any more!

Now..why the four stars instead of five? Well, four is still good. Even three is good. Because, although it says Soft Bounce, it was harder than I imagined. At this time, bouncing with both feet is uncomfortable for ME. My legs throb and ache. So, I've gotten around that by doing a sort of dance 'Twist'; some Jumping Jack type moves and hops and that seems to do the trick. Am I just more out of shape than I thought? Will it eventually improve? I don't know. I'll let you know.
I can't help but wish that I were able to COMPARE my rebounders bounce/feel with other rebounders of EQUAL or GREATER value in order to see if another would've been more comfortable for me, but I'll not ever have that opportunity to do so; and this was my price range and I am content with it and would recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce

text_fidelity_a:
BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids. I purchased this to use on my bicycle that I use for commuting. I leave early in the morning while it is still dark. The route I take is pretty well lit with street lights so I use the lights mostly for visibility and not to light the road in front of me.

The mounts are pretty simple to use. I attached the front to the handlebar and the back to the basket I have on the rear rack. The front light has 3 steady settings at 3 levels of brightness and one flashing mode. I am not sure how useful the level of brightness would be in absolute darkness as far as seeing the path in front of you because I have not used it in that scenario, but it seems pretty bright to me. I keep it on flashing mode for visibility. It is conveniently re-chargeable via USB cord and it seems to last adequately between charges.

I gave this product a 3 star rating because the back light does not work the way I need it to. The first time I used it, I thought I turned it on but when I got to my destination it was off so I figured I forgot to turn it on. The second time I used it on the return trip, I made absolutely sure it was on when I started and when I got to the destination it was off again. I took the light off my bike and turned it on and dropped it onto a hard surface from a distance of less than 3 inches and it shut off. Since this is battery operated and not rechargeable, I'm guessing the batteries get jolted from going over a bump on the road and shuts off on its own. It lights up again without any issues if you press the on button again, but that is not feasible or safe to reach behind you and fix it if you are riding on a road with vehicular traffic all around you. It is also very inconvenient to pull over to the side every time it shuts off to turn it back on again. Since the light set was fairly inexpensive, I just purchased a different separate backlight from the local box store to replace it.

I will not go through the time and inconvenience of returning the item or exchanging it because it simply is not worth it. I hope the seller doesn't try to contact me to "fix" the problem because they will be wasting their time.
text_fidelity_b: BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids.

text_fidelity_a:
Michelin A1 Aircomp Ultralight Fahrrad Schlauch 28´´ I bought two of these at Performance bike shop because they were on sale. Smooth stems looked nice.
Both of them came apart at the seam. One lasted a few miles from home, another lasted little longer but otherwise more walking distance to home. I had a patch kit and a pump but no use. At least I got refund when took them back to the store. I explained the store clerk what had happened and he wasn't even surprised.
I had different brands of tubes mostly cheap store brand in the past but nothing compare to this. I was very surprised because this happened to well-known name.
What I learned from this. 1) Don't buy anything says ultra light. 2) Don't buy anything only because it's a well-known brand name, it was probably made by another company.
I weigh 140lbs, so the weight wasn't an issue, just in case you are wondering. I inflated it 120psi. Size of the tire was 700x20c.
You can avoid pinch flat snake bites by inflating the tire to certain pressure. If the tire picks up a broken staple, it gets flat but you can patch it. When the tube comes apart, you can't do anything specially if the spare you happen to have has the same defect.

I'll never buy it and I don't recommend this to anybody.
text_fidelity_b: Michelin A1 Aircomp Ultralight Fahrrad Schlauch 28´´

Goplus Fitness Hyper Extension Hyperextension Bench Chair Workout Core Abdominal My official review on YouTube is a 3.5 but half stars don't fly on Amazon. For a video version check this out: https://youtu.be/abd0bJ7ZMiQ

Pros:
-Cost.
-Shipping speed.
-Quality with cost factored in.
-Works well for home gym purposes.

Cons:
-Awful instructions.
-Adjustability is limited.
-Light commercial would be a stretch based on the design of the ankle supports.

The cons are a bit strong because the instructions are not step by step. It's basically a build sheet so some trial and error will occur when assembling. Other than the ankle support and adjustability this could be light commercial but the ankle support is very wobbly. The adjustability is limited as well even for a hyperextension (I'm 5'8" and use the closest notch). To do GHRs I'd have to drill a few more holes around 4 inches closer.

Overall it's a solid buy and I'd recommend its purchase based on the price. I've had the lower prices Roman chair on Amazon (around $65) and it was much more lightweight than this.

Would easily recommend!

text_fidelity_a: Portable Dual Burner Alcohol Stove Alcohol Heater Burner with Glass Kettle for Tea Coffee Maker Outdoor Backpacking Picnic Camping Hiking Korean BBQ I live in Texas and in the February blizzard we had last year, I was stuck in my home without power for 5 days.  20 degrees outside, it was around 34 inside...for 5 days.  I did turn on my water faucets so that my pipes did not freeze and burst, and I was lucky enough to have a loaf of bread, peanut butter & jelly, and powdered milk.  So, in the months and months since then, I have gotten solar panels, a 200 amp hour LifePO4 battery, a 3000 watt inverter...but also have camp stoves run with propane, a propane heater and now this really nice little alcohol burner.  I also have a couple of mini-firepits that use 99% alcohol for fuel which is what this little burner uses as well.  I can at least boil water on this little burner with the power out, but with the included screen, it can be used outside as well (with the screen keeping any breeze from causing a problem).  When wondering how long you may be in the dark during a power outage, having a couple of solar lights and a way to heat up soup or make coffee on this little burner gives me peace of mind.  I love the carry case - I do have a propane cook stove that has a carrier and that makes it easy to store them both for the next time I need to use them.  I do think the price is a bit high, but again, having "redundancy" in emergency situations is important to me and I'm happy with adding this burner to my emergency use for heating food/drinks.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Dual Burner Alcohol Stove Alcohol Heater Burner with Glass Kettle for Tea Coffee Maker Outdoor Backpacking Picnic Camping Hiking Korean BBQ

text_fidelity_a:
Perfect Fitness Bands Pro with Tendon Tech The tendon tech band is a little piece of equipment that so far seems pretty decent for convenient resistance-type workouts. Time will tell how well it holds up.

Pros:

It is compact and light--easy to bring along when traveling

illustrations of workout moves are available on line

So far it seems pretty strong. The resistance level is high--you can certainly feel the tension during and afterward you can feel the effect

It is very easy to change resistance--simply move your hands closer together on the band. The change is pretty immediate (in other words, you don't have to shift your hands very much to feel a difference, meaning you should be able to work your way up over time) and highly noticeable.

The material is easy to maintain a grip on

it feels durable, but as mentioned, only time can really tell

Cons
Not really very many. The biggest complaint I have is that there isn't any guide (even a rough one) as to what the resistance is the equivalent of, as you usually find on resistance bands.

Seems slightly cheap to not include a simple guide to workouts with the band itself (not a big deal though as you'll quickly learn them and wouldn't use a paper anyway)

While the band is easy to grip, it isn't always a comfortable grip. Again, a very minor complaint as usually you just need to work your hands around a bit to get more comfortable

So far, so good
text_fidelity_b: Perfect Fitness Bands Pro with Tendon Tech

text_fidelity_a:
PodiuMax Portable Extendable Flexible Soccer Field Fence, Kids Playpen Safety Activity Centre, Easy Assemble and Disassemble, 8 Panels per Set, for Indoor and Outdoor This comes in a very long heavy box. In the box are:

- 16 long tubes
- 16 short tubes
- 32 right angles
- 8 nets
- 16 two-way clips
- 4 flathead grooved base
- 4 Phillips head grooved base

Installation is easy in the sense that all I had to do was insert the long poles on the top and bottom of each net and the short poles on the side into the channels. However, strength is required to seat the final set of right angles on each panel. The Velcroed end gets inserted last. Finally, the Velcro strap goes around the post and net (see photo) to keep that channel secure.

Although the installation was easy, it took me about three hours because it was very tedious and repetitive and there were so many parts. In the end I wound up with eight panels. The clips are used to clip the panels together and they turn on the tube so that the fences can be configured into a quad configuration, a square, or just a haphazard fence as I did in my photos.  The rubber bases just hold the fence upright as long as it is not too windy. In the wind, the fence bends with the direction of the blow.

The fence can be folded for storage at the joints. The only thing is the bases are heavy and need to be carried separately. For the current price of $299.99, it would have been great if they included a bag to carry the bases in. Nevertheless, this fence is excellent and delivers as described.
text_fidelity_b: PodiuMax Portable Extendable Flexible Soccer Field Fence, Kids Playpen Safety Activity Centre, Easy Assemble and Disassemble, 8 Panels per Set, for Indoor and Outdoor

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E902 Air Walk Trainer Elliptical Machine Glider w/LCD Monitor, 220 LB Max Weight and 30 Inch Stride My husband just bought me the Sunny Air Walk Trainer, and it arrived yesterday. The box was so damaged that we were concerned there might be damage to the unit, but everything was fine. My husband had it put together in 10 minutes, leaving off the pad at my request. It's very quiet, quiet enough to chat over in a low voice, and the action is smooth. The time/distance display works fine, although I'd have rather it showed distance rather than number of individual motions back and forth.

This gives a no-impact workout, which is great if you're prone to shin splits or have bad knees. Unlike a lot of other fitness equipment, the foot pedals stay level with the floor, sort of like roller skating, which I find a big plus. On the other hand, I'm only 5' 3", but the stride is on the short side for me; not too short, but it took a little time to adjust. There's no resistance, so while it did get my heart pumping, I wouldn't think this would be as useful for someone fit who does a lot of cardio. For someone like me, recovering and overweight, it's fine.

One thing worth considering is that whenever you walk, jog or run, your weight is off each foot as you lift it to take the next step. With the Sunny Air Walk Trainer - or any other similar unit including the Gazelle - your weight is constantly on both feet. If you're overweight or have weak knees, this may be a concern.

The Air Walk Trainer is fairly well made - much better than I expected. It's also nice and small. I didn't even bother to fold it up - just pushed it into a corner. And this has to be one of the best values in fitness equipment - under $100, strong, made of metal, smooth action. If you don't have room for a treadmill or recumbent exercise bike and are looking for a lighter workout, I'd definitely consider this.

BTW, I'll update this review after I've had the Air Walk Trainer for a while.

Edit: After using this for a few months, I sold my Air Walk Trainer because I found that even at 5' 3", the stride is too short for me to really get going. Years ago, I had a Gazelle, and with that, I was able to use my full stride of 22", but with the reduced stride length of the Air Walk Trainer, I always felt constrained. Still, if that doesn't bother you, it's a decent piece of equipment. For my use, I'd give this 3 stars, but for others who don't mind shortening their stride, it's a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E902 Air Walk Trainer Elliptical Machine Glider w/LCD Monitor, 220 LB Max Weight and 30 Inch Stride

text_fidelity_a:
Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs I’ll be honest, I’d never heard about exercise plate machines until I saw this one. I looked it up and according to the articles I was reading, this is an under used exercise machine type and actually does help loose weight. So I decided to grab this LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine and try it. I come away surprised, but happy - it does help me. My wife and I have been active in living a healthier lifestyle and approach with a variety of activities, from kickboxing and walking to weights to... well, this thing. My wife is still sidelined from her severely broken foot, so she has not tried it yet, but I have and I’m blown away by how it works.

The machine arrives in a box that is easy to remove from - all the parts are fit correctly and easy to get out. It is slightly heavy - nothing one can’t move, but it has some weight to it. I’m not sure the actual size, but we can’t fit it under our bed, so we’re still working on where to keep it - but that’s not an issue. There are instructions - I would suggest also doing a little research. I learned a few things from articles I was reading. There are also resistance bands and for your arms resistance ropes as well. The instructions are well done and offer ideas for working out as well.

The unit has a remote so you don’t have to get off or bend down to alter things. I have used it every time - I will increase or decrease the various options while still on it. This comes in handy for severity of the vibration as it is intense and I’ll inch it up or down during the workout. I have not gone very high - I want to say around 15 - and appreciate being able to try things or adjust as I need.

ONE CON: The power cord is short. I have to use it primarily in our bedroom where my wife is currently working from bed, so that limits when I can use it. If it were at least another 2 - 3 feet long it would be perfect. I’m going to move some things around and try to make it work in the living room, but if not... anyways, if they changed that this would be a perfect unit.

I really love the workout. It is... (not) easy. I mean you’re standing on this vibrating plate and you do feel it. The level, the time, going up and down, the truth is, your body works to stay there. I’ve only stood on it and done planks, and both were workouts. I got off sweating. I’ll say, standing on it is less of a vibration to my head than the plank - I can’t go as long or as high at a single time because in the plank position I feel like my head will vibrate off. But I can feel my core working.

I like this unit so much that when I saw a foot massager from the same company I grabbed it. text_fidelity_a:
Contigo AUTOSEAL Grace Reusable Water Bottle, 24oz, Citron First off, let me start by saying that I am a loyal Contigo customer. I absolutely LOVE my Contigo Autoseal West Loop Stainless Steel Travel Mug with Easy-Clean Lid, and sing its praises frequently. I purchased the Grace water bottle to throw in my day pack when working at my son's cub scout camp. Here are the reasons I chose it:

1. It's Contigo. I like their beverage containers, and they have wonderful customer service - they stand behind their products.
2. It was $10.40.
3. It's BPA-free plastic, and doesn't feel flimsy. I love my stainless steel mug, but since I'm going to be using this primarily in the woods, I didn't want to risk dropping my steel mug on the ground and breaking it.
2. It's easy to fill with both water and ice. We have water stations set up around camp, and I generally fill the bottle at home in the morning with ice, and refill throughout the day with water.
4. It's a streamlined design, and doesn't take up much room in my pack.
5. It doesn't leak when filled properly (note - you have to be attentive to where you fill the bottle - you don't want to fill it above the shoulder, or the bottle will likely leak).
6. It's easy to use & drink from.
7. It's generally easy to clean and has no funky odors.
8. It fits into my car's cup holders.

Here are things that would make it better:
1. Adding a carabineer to the loop, or having built-in carabineer as part of the loop for clipping onto a day pack or bag, similar to some of Contigo's other Autoseal bottles. I've done this for my bottle, but I had to purchase this separately.
2. Double-wall insulation. The thing I love about my stainless Contigo mug is that it keeps my coffee hot and my iced drinks cold (and my ice cubes from melting) for hours - with no transference of the heat/cold to the outer wall of the mug. The Grace bottle does not keep water cold, and it will "sweat" when it's filled with iced drinks.
3. Having an "easy clean" lid. My stainless travel mug (are you sensing a theme, here?) has a fantastic easy clean lid, with parts that swing out on hinges to get into all the crevices, ensuring a better cleaning.

But this bottle was $10.40, not $25. And for that price and my purposes, it works, and I'm happy with it!

Note - I purchased a Contigo Cortland water bottle with easy-clean lid for my son a few months ago, and it has begun to leak. I called Contigo, and they told me that this is a known issue with the Cortland design - not the design I am reviewing here. After I fill out their form and submit two pictures of the bottle (one of the lid, one of the entire bottle), they will replace it for me, even though I don't have the receipt anymore (it was not purchased through Amazon). Again - Contigo has great customer service!
text_fidelity_b: Contigo AUTOSEAL Grace Reusable Water Bottle, 24oz, Citron

text_fidelity_a:
Nathan Unisex Hydration Back-Pack for Running, Hiking, Cycling and more. 2L Bladder Included / 6L Storage Capacity. Adjustable Straps. NO BOUNCE while Running. I purchased this vest 6 years ago and it served me well in multiple ultras. It has just enough space for everything you need. I just checked the front zip pocket and it's just a tad too small for my Samsung Galaxy S7 Active, which is a thick phone. It definitely wouldn't fit an iPhone 6-7 Plus. The pack rides low enough on your back that there are no real issues with rubbing or chafing of the neck...from the pack. I did get a bit annoyed from time to time by the hose rubbing my neck, though. The side straps....what can I say? Over 6 years, I've never figured out how to adjust them well, lol. But it hasn't seemed to matter much. For a while, I used to over-cinch the chest strap but realized it can stay pretty loose and the pack is still not very bouncy. The front right pocket is where I've always tucked my phone. Although I admit sometimes I've used a SpiBelt with this pack to free up more pocket space for gels. You don't get a whole lot of space in the back pocket but it's perfect for those rarely used but "just in case" items I like to bring like an emergency poncho, extra sunscreen, lip balm, ginger chews, etc.

The bite valve on Nathan's bladder tube has always been problematic for me. I never really "bit" it hard yet within a year or so, it began to leak. After one race, my leg was covered in syrupy goo where gatorade and leaked and evaporated over the course of 50 miles. I swapped it out for the bite valve from a Camelbak and never had another problem. Like all bladders, be religious about cleaning this one post-use or it will gunk up very quickly. The closure system on the bladder takes some getting use to. You'll become a pro at it but for years I watched aid station volunteers stare in bewilderment, trying to figure out how to open it. More often than not, I ended up doing it myself.

I used to find after 100 milers that the top of my back would have a slightly chaffed feel to it, without anything being rubbed raw. I'm sure a light application of body glide or vasoline would have prevented that. But overall, this is a great, basic vest with plenty of fluid capacity. I recently replaced mine with Nathan's VaporAir, mainly for more pockets. But I could easily have bought this again and been happy.
text_fidelity_b: Nathan Unisex Hydration Back-Pack for Running, Hiking, Cycling and more. 2L Bladder Included / 6L Storage Capacity. Adjustable Straps. NO BOUNCE while Running.

text_fidelity_a:
Mountain House Classic Chili Mac with Beef | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food | 3 Servings I have tried a number of mountain house meals, and absolutely adore the fact that they have a 30 year shelf life, really sturdy solid packaging, and that they are so easy to prepare. They are also incredibly delicious! When rehydrated, the quality level tastes like something you would get from a roadside diner, which is to say, really very tasty in kind of a lowbrow way.

I shared this chili mac and beef entrée with my children. We had it with some vegetables from the garden on the side to freshen it up, because there aren't really any vegetables in here. There were ample enough portions of meat and pasta, and enough sauce and flavoring to go around. I was really impressed with how well they managed to bring all of the flavors together, and how well everything rehydrated.

I will advise that you should definitely use the hottest boiling water possible to make this, because I found that when my water is merely simmering when I pour it in, sometimes the center of the meat chunks or bigger pieces do not rehydrate as well as I would hope. However, when done as directed, these really are great.

The portion size was generous enough to feed a 40-year-old woman (myself) and two small children, with a pile of vegetables on the side. If you are not having vegetables on the side, I would not try to share.
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Classic Chili Mac with Beef | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food | 3 Servings

text_fidelity_a:
KastKing Sharky Baitfeeder III Spinning Reel 10+1 Shielded Stainless Steel BB - Carbon Fiber Drag for Live Liner Bait Fishing Action I don't write many reviews - typically when I do they are positive. I'm pretty disappointed. My wife bought me this this reel to go fishing with my kids for Father's Day. I had been reading about these Kastking bait feeders and it was much less expensive than a known Shimano. I watched some youtube videos about it that seemed pretty good and the amazon reviews seemed real good. We got to the pier and I had them spool it up with 20# mono. I like having my spools wound by the machine - it does a better job. The drag cap came off but it was difficult to remove. It seems like it took a good 2 minutes to unscrew... NOW it will not go back on - it freely spins and won't attach.
I posted a photo I can't tell if it's stripped or what is going on inside there. The threading appears to be fine.
The old timers that work at the pier fooled with it but said that's what I get for buying unknown name brands. I told them everyone started out unknown! I recently bought a penn battle II rod / reel combo and the rod was defective from the factory.
I wasted my $6 to get her spooled up with line but the worst part I didn't get to try out my new reel on father's day - I was really excited to use it! I'm glad I didn't get the other spool loaded up with braided line like I was thinking - I'd have been out another $30...
If the Kastking people make good on the replacement I'll test it out and will consider changing my rating. Right now I'm disappointed and wanted to gripe. Anticlimactic!
Is this rare or typical? We'll find out! Looking at other ratings seems like it might be rare (I hope). I'll update as things progress. - Wayne
text_fidelity_b: KastKing Sharky Baitfeeder III Spinning Reel 10+1 Shielded Stainless Steel BB - Carbon Fiber Drag for Live Liner Bait Fishing Action

The setup instructions are meager and I would recommend the manufacturer put more detailed instructions on the web.

I have used it maybe a dozen times so far. Clean up is easy. Turning it on is a breeze. I had never used a small propane grill but the hook up is simple. You find the 1 pound propane bottles in all the larger stores.

The weird thing is that the legs are not long enough for the propane bottle so you must be able to put the grill on surface that allows the bottle to hang off the end.

You can adapt the fuel to a larger fuel source but that defeats the purpose of the portability.

Heats up super quick. VERY light weight. I have easily cooked 4 steaks one meal, 6 burgers another, 6 chicken breasts another, a dozen hot dogs another as well as 4 pork chops and 4 sauce last night.

The drip tray is easy to remove and clean.

The travel bag is super a mesh side pocket for the gas canister, but you don't want to put a dirty grill in it and bring home to clean - the bag will not be pretty. The lid latches and the legs fold for storage in the bag .

The stainless steel looks great and the bag is terrific for storage and reducing scratches - the product seems durable - I'll let you know if I am still using in a couple years.

I got this mostly for emergency needs but found myself addicted to the ease of grilling quickly and without a fuss.

Just getting back into cycling this year after decades away, and everything has changed, right down to the solvents and lubes. Finish Line Dry amazes me - the drivetrain stays clean for multiple long rides even through dusty conditions. Since I switched to dry I spend less time cleaning and lubing my bike and more time on the fun stuff.

BTW the bottle says it's not recommended for wet/muddy conditions and I believe them. I will try Finish Line Wet when my old aerosol wet lube runs out.

EDIT: I've progressed quite a bit as a rider and as a wrench. I've come back to this lube after a tour of what's available. It does work fine in the rain. I learned this trick at the local bike shop: squirt it onto a clean shop rag instead of directly on the chain. Run the chain through the rag do wipe in the new lube and wipe away collected grime. Drivetrain maintenance just keeps getting easier!

text_fidelity_a:
BARWING 10-7-4-3 Weight Bench Adjustable Exercise | 800 LB Heavy Incline Decline Bench Press for Home Gym More Stable and Posture Adjustments | 5 Min Easy Assembly Foldable Training Lifting Bench | Dragon Flag Handle for Abdominal Arm Workout First off, I read through all of the reviews that are 3 stars and lower (up to the point that this review is posted) and they are all unfair, likely written by people that do not read through item descriptions thoroughly before buying/read the user manual before using.

Those that are complaining that the bench is not big enough for them to do their specific exercise(s), the DIMENSIONS are in the description! That's YOUR fault for not reading and determining that this product will not work for your needs.

And to those complaining that it is not quick/easy to adjust, the manual tells you to loosen the locking knobs (takes me about 2-3 full twists) and then PULL the end of the knob with one hand and adjust the bench with the other. That's how the quick-lock works. It is even etched into each of the knobs. Then the knob "automatically" finds the next hole as you move the bench cushion, and then you twist it tight to secure. It is not even slightly difficult. If you're having problems with this, you should probably start with some hand grip exercises before you start lifting weights on this thing.

Now, for the product itself. This bench met all of my expectations. It's heavy, sturdy, versatile, made of durable metal, took about 5 minutes to setup initially out of the box, and easy to adjust and collapse for storing. The gray stitching around the sides LOOKS like it is made of flimsy material and that it will rip easily, but I did a pull test all the way around, and unless you're trying to intentionally destroy this thing it's going to last a good while.

I only have 2 complaints. One, mine came with slight damage (scratch in the metal with rust, see pics) that doesn't affect the functionality at all. Second, when fully collapsed, the bench doesn't sit upright and has to be leaned against a wall like the lady does in the video, or you extend the leg pads so that it rests on them and balances on itself (see pic for a better description). Both of these are certainly not deal breakers.

All in all, I am happy with my purchase. The price is very fair for the quality! These negative reviewers are likely looking for a handout or unnecessary apology from a company doing great things out here.
text_fidelity_b: BARWING 10-7-4-3 Weight Bench Adjustable Exercise | 800 LB Heavy Incline Decline Bench Press for Home Gym More Stable and Posture Adjustments | 5 Min Easy Assembly Foldable Training Lifting Bench | Dragon Flag Handle for Abdominal Arm Workout

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick I've previously owned a Klymit V without the "Luxe," but a piece of the one valve it had broke off in short order. This Klymit V Luxe has valves which *appear* to me to have fewer fiddly parts, and there are two of them--more on why that's good in a moment!

First off, these pads have a smart design. Although there is no railing per say, the Vs help to keep you on them which is good news if you do not stay in one place on a bed. The material keeps the air inside from feeling cold (and presumably from drinking in too much of the earth's cold).

The primary use I gave my original V was as a buffer between me and an extremely ill-suited new mattress while I desperately shopped for solutions. And although I've been a backpacker in the past, sadly, my primary intended use for the Static V Luxe is to act as a buffering layer when I need to sleep on other people's mattresses. I have considerable back health issues, and this padding is incredibly helpful for when I cannot be on my own mattress. I purchased this size this time because the original V is so much smaller than a twin bed that it was downright silly trying to use it for my purpose. Also I use a body pillow and change positions a lot. This will clearly be nicer for managing nights out of my own bed.

Now I saw someone complaining about the two valves because they are confusing. This person has probably never experienced the downsides of only having one valve for letting air out of a mattress. Sure, you need to be certain that the valve you are not blowing into is closed so that the mattress can properly inflate, but oh, my word, it is soooooo much easier to get the air out of this mattress pad! I could almost never get my original V small enough to properly stick into its dry sack. But this larger V luxe easily packs up smaller than I could get the original V to go. Ok, so maybe "easy" is relative. You do need to open both valves, roll it down from bottom to top, open it up again, fold a few times, and roll once more to get it maximally small. But it actually works and stuffs in the drysack.

I hope if you're reading this that you have more adventurous uses afoot, but I do recommend this Static V Luxe and wish I'd had one back when I was a backpacker!
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick
